```{r}
convertMNEtoVariables <- function(MNE, skeleton, individuals = NULL) {

  if (length(MNE) != nrow(skeleton)) {
    stop("Length of MNE vector must match the number of skeletal elements")
  }

  # Convert MNE to a data frame if it's not already
  if (!is.data.frame(MNE)) {
    MNE <- as.data.frame(MNE)
  }

  Element <- skeleton$element

  # Calculate MNI and Individuals if not provided
  if (is.null(individuals)) {
    MNI <- ceiling(MNE$MNE / skeleton$count)
    individuals <- max(MNI)
  }

  # Compute Abundance for each part
  abundance <- MNE$MNE / (skeleton$count * individuals)

  # Compute Mean Abundance (MA)
  ma <- sum(MNE$MNE, na.rm = TRUE) / (sum(skeleton$count, na.rm = TRUE) * individuals)

  # Compute Mean Part Abundance (MPA)
    mpa <- sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / length(abundance)

  # Additional metrics calculations
  MAU <- abundance
  MNAU <- abundance
  PMAU <- MAU / max(MNE$MNE / skeleton$count)
  PMNAU <- MNAU / individuals
  ReMNAU <- MNAU / sum(MNAU, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Calculate Accumulative ReMNAU
  AcReMNAU <- cumsum(ReMNAU)

  # Bone level vector calculation using summarize_bone_sections
  #bone_info_df <- data.frame(elements = skeleton$Element, counts = MNE$MNE)
  #bone_level <- c(1,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2)

  # Return a list of all calculated metrics
  return(list(
    MNE = as.vector(MNE$MNE),
    Elements = Element,
    abundance = abundance,
    MNI = individuals,
    MAU = MAU,
    MNAU = MNAU,
    PercentMAU = PMAU,
    PercentMNAU = PMNAU,
    ReMNAU = ReMNAU,
    AcReMNAU = AcReMNAU,
    MeanAbundance = ma,
    MeanPartAbundance = mpa
    #bone_level = bone_level
  ))
}
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Assuming your tibble is called 'recalc_data'
# Step 1: Create a helper function that applies `convertMNEtoVariables` to each row.
apply_conversion <- function(count, bone_level, number_of_individuals) {
  skeleton <- get_bones_dataframe(bone_level)
  result <- convertMNEtoVariables(count, skeleton, number_of_individuals)
  
  # Return the list of computed values you want to add to the dataframe
  return(result)
}

# Step 2: Use `pmap` to apply the function to each row and add computed values as new columns
# Here we assume your 'count', 'bone.level', and 'number_of_individuals' columns contain lists, as in your example.
recalc_data <- grouped_data %>%
  mutate(
    results = pmap(
      list(count = count, bone_level = bone.level, number_of_individuals = number_of_individuals),
      apply_conversion
    )
  )

# Step 3: Extract specific metrics from the results and add them as new columns
recalc_data <- recalc_data %>%
  mutate(
    MNE = map(results, ~.x$MNE),
    Elements = map(results, ~.x$Elements),
    abundance = map(results, ~.x$abundance),
    MNI = map(results, ~.x$MNI),
    MAU = map(results, ~.x$MAU),
    PercentMAU = map(results, ~.x$PercentMAU),
    AcReMNAU = map(results, ~.x$AcReMNAU),
    MeanAbundance = map(results, ~.x$MeanAbundance),
    MeanPartAbundance = map(results, ~.x$MeanPartAbundance)
  ) %>%
  select(-results)  # Optionally remove the intermediate 'results' column if you don't need it
```

```{r}
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)

# Assuming 'recalc_data' is your dataframe

# Columns to check for identical entries
columns_to_check <- c("time_range", "geological_context", "accumulation_cause", 
                      "gender", "age", "hominin_species")

# Identify columns with identical entries
identical_entries <- sapply(recalc_data[columns_to_check], function(x) length(unique(x)) == 1)
identical_columns <- names(identical_entries[identical_entries == TRUE])

# Get unique values of these columns for the title, excluding "mixed"
title_entries <- sapply(identical_columns, function(col) {
  val <- unique(recalc_data[[col]])
  if (val != "mixed") {
    return(val)
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
})
# Remove NULL entries
title_entries <- title_entries[!sapply(title_entries, is.null)]

# Create the title
if (length(title_entries) > 0) {
  title <- paste(title_entries, collapse = " ")
  title <- paste(title, "sites")
} else {
  title <- "Sites"
}

# Get the names of all columns before the 'sum' column
all_columns <- names(recalc_data)
sum_index <- which(all_columns == "sum")
label_columns <- all_columns[1:(sum_index - 1)]

# Create labels by merging entries of columns before 'sum', excluding "mixed"
labels <- apply(recalc_data[label_columns], 1, function(row) {
  row <- row[row != "mixed"]
  paste(row, collapse = " ")
})

# Initialize plot
fig <- plot_ly()

# Get elements (assuming same for all rows)
elements <- recalc_data$Elements[[1]]

# Ensure elements are factors with levels in the desired order
elements_factor <- factor(elements, levels = elements)

# Metrics to plot
metrics <- c("MNE", "MAU", "PercentMAU", "AcReMNAU")

# Total number of traces
num_metrics <- length(metrics)
num_rows <- nrow(recalc_data)
total_traces <- num_metrics * num_rows

# Initialize visibility matrix
visibility_matrix <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = num_metrics, ncol = total_traces)

# Initialize trace counter
trace_counter <- 1

for (metric_index in seq_along(metrics)) {
  metric <- metrics[metric_index]
  
  for (row_index in 1:num_rows) {
    y_values <- recalc_data[[metric]][[row_index]]
    x_values <- recalc_data$Elements[[row_index]]
    
    # Ensure x_values have the same order as 'elements'
    x_values_factor <- factor(x_values, levels = elements)
    
    # Add trace with mode = 'lines+markers'
    fig <- fig %>%
      add_trace(x = x_values_factor, y = y_values,
                mode = 'lines+markers',
                type = 'scatter',
                name = labels[row_index],
                visible = ifelse(metric == "MNE", TRUE, FALSE))
    
    # Update visibility matrix
    visibility_matrix[metric_index, trace_counter] <- TRUE
    
    trace_counter <- trace_counter + 1
  }
}

# Create buttons for each metric
buttons_list <- list()
for (metric_index in seq_along(metrics)) {
  metric <- metrics[metric_index]
  
  # Create visibility vector
  visibility <- as.vector(visibility_matrix[metric_index, ])
  
  button <- list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(list(visible = visibility)),
    label = metric
  )
  
  buttons_list[[metric_index]] <- button
}

# Place buttons at the bottom
updatemenus <- list(
  list(
    type = "buttons",
    direction = "left",
    xanchor = 'center',
    yanchor = 'bottom',
    x = 0.5,
    y = -0.2,
    showactive = TRUE,
    buttons = buttons_list
  )
)

# Final layout
fig <- fig %>%
  layout(
    title = title,
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Element",
      type = 'category',
      categoryorder = "array",
      categoryarray = elements
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = "Value"),
    updatemenus = updatemenus
  )

# Display the plot
fig
```

```{r}
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Function to perform PCA and create a plot for a given metric
perform_pca_and_plot <- function(data_column, metric_name) {
  # Unnest the column for the metric
  data_matrix <- recalc_data %>%
    select({{data_column}}) %>%
    unnest(cols = {{data_column}}) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  # Ensure the data has enough rows and columns for PCA
  if (ncol(data_matrix) > 1) {
    # Perform PCA
    pca_result <- prcomp(data_matrix, scale = TRUE)
    
    # Extract the first two principal components
    num_pc <- min(ncol(pca_result$x), 2)  # Check the number of available PCs
    pca_data <- as_tibble(pca_result$x[, 1:num_pc])
    colnames(pca_data) <- paste0("PC", 1:num_pc)
    
    # Add original labels (like geological context and accumulation cause)
    pca_data <- pca_data %>%
      mutate(geological_context = recalc_data$geological_context[rep(1:nrow(recalc_data), each = length(recalc_data[[metric_name]][[1]]))],
             accumulation_cause = recalc_data$accumulation_cause[rep(1:nrow(recalc_data), each = length(recalc_data[[metric_name]][[1]]))],
             label = paste(geological_context, accumulation_cause))
    
    # Plot the first two PCs using plotly
    fig <- plot_ly(pca_data, x = ~PC1, y = ~ifelse(num_pc == 2, PC2, 0), type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers', 
                   color = ~label, text = ~label,
                   marker = list(size = 10)) %>%
      layout(title = paste("PCA of", metric_name),
             xaxis = list(title = "PC1"),
             yaxis = list(title = ifelse(num_pc == 2, "PC2", "Only PC1 available")))
    
    return(fig)
  } else {
    return(print(paste("Insufficient data for PCA for", metric_name)))
  }
}

# Perform PCA and plot for each metric
fig_mne <- perform_pca_and_plot(MNE, "MNE")
fig_mau <- perform_pca_and_plot(MAU, "MAU")
fig_percentmau <- perform_pca_and_plot(PercentMAU, "PercentMAU")
fig_acremnau <- perform_pca_and_plot(AcReMNAU, "AcReMNAU")

# Show the plots
fig_mne  # Plot for MNE
fig_mau  # Plot for MAU
fig_percentmau  # Plot for PercentMAU
fig_acremnau  # Plot for AcReMNAU

```

```{r}
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Function to perform PCA and prepare a data frame for plotting
perform_pca <- function(data, label_column) {
  pca_result <- prcomp(data, scale = TRUE)
  pca_data <- as_tibble(pca_result$x[, 1:2]) # Take only the first two principal components
  colnames(pca_data) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  
  # Add label to the PCA data (e.g., geological context, accumulation cause)
  pca_data <- pca_data %>%
    mutate(label = label_column)
  
  return(pca_data)
}

# Create PCA data for each metric separately

# PCA for MNE
mne_data <- recalc_data %>% 
  select(MNE) %>%
  unnest(cols = MNE) %>%
  as.matrix()
pca_mne <- perform_pca(mne_data, recalc_data$geological_context)

# PCA for MAU
mau_data <- recalc_data %>% 
  select(MAU) %>%
  unnest(cols = MAU) %>%
  as.matrix()
pca_mau <- perform_pca(mau_data, recalc_data$geological_context)

# PCA for PercentMAU
percentmau_data <- recalc_data %>% 
  select(PercentMAU) %>%
  unnest(cols = PercentMAU) %>%
  as.matrix()
pca_percentmau <- perform_pca(percentmau_data, recalc_data$geological_context)

# PCA for AcReMNAU
acre_mnau_data <- recalc_data %>% 
  select(AcReMNAU) %>%
  unnest(cols = AcReMNAU) %>%
  as.matrix()
pca_acre_mnau <- perform_pca(acre_mnau_data, recalc_data$geological_context)

# Initialize plot
fig <- plot_ly()

# Add traces for MNE PCA
fig <- fig %>%
  add_trace(x = pca_mne$PC1, y = pca_mne$PC2, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers',
            marker = list(size = 10), name = 'MNE PCA', visible = TRUE,
            text = ~pca_mne$label)

# Add traces for MAU PCA
fig <- fig %>%
  add_trace(x = pca_mau$PC1, y = pca_mau$PC2, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers',
            marker = list(size = 10), name = 'MAU PCA', visible = FALSE,
            text = ~pca_mau$label)

# Add traces for PercentMAU PCA
fig <- fig %>%
  add_trace(x = pca_percentmau$PC1, y = pca_percentmau$PC2, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers',
            marker = list(size = 10), name = 'PercentMAU PCA', visible = FALSE,
            text = ~pca_percentmau$label)

# Add traces for AcReMNAU PCA
fig <- fig %>%
  add_trace(x = pca_acre_mnau$PC1, y = pca_acre_mnau$PC2, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers',
            marker = list(size = 10), name = 'AcReMNAU PCA', visible = FALSE,
            text = ~pca_acre_mnau$label)

# Create buttons to toggle between different PCA plots
buttons_list <- list(
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(list(visible = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE))),
    label = "MNE PCA"
  ),
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(list(visible = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))),
    label = "MAU PCA"
  ),
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(list(visible = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))),
    label = "PercentMAU PCA"
  ),
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(list(visible = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))),
    label = "AcReMNAU PCA"
  )
)

# Layout with buttons
fig <- fig %>%
  layout(
    title = "PCA for MNE, MAU, PercentMAU, AcReMNAU",
    xaxis = list(title = "PC1"),
    yaxis = list(title = "PC2"),
    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        type = "buttons",
        direction = "left",
        xanchor = 'center',
        yanchor = 'top',
        x = 0.5,
        y = 1.15,
        buttons = buttons_list
      )
    )
  )

# Show the plot
fig

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Perform PCA and prepare a data frame for plotting
perform_pca <- function(data) {
  pca_result <- prcomp(data, scale = TRUE)
  pca_data <- as_tibble(pca_result$x[, 1:2]) # Take only the first two principal components
  colnames(pca_data) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  
  # Add label to the PCA data (e.g., geological context, accumulation cause)
  pca_data$label <- rownames(data)
  
  return(pca_data)
}

# Process MNE, MAU, and PercentMAU data
mne_data <- recalc_data %>%
  select(MNE) %>%
  unnest_wider(MNE, names_sep = "_") %>%
  as.matrix()

mau_data <- recalc_data %>%
  select(MAU) %>%
  unnest_wider(MAU, names_sep = "_") %>%
  as.matrix()

percentmau_data <- recalc_data %>%
  select(PercentMAU) %>%
  unnest_wider(PercentMAU, names_sep = "_") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Generate labels
all_columns <- names(recalc_data)
sum_index <- which(all_columns == "sum")
label_columns <- all_columns[1:(sum_index - 1)]

rownames(mau_data) <- labels
rownames(percentmau_data) <- labels

pca_mau <- perform_pca(mau_data)
pca_percentmau <- perform_pca(percentmau_data)

  } else {

  }
})

# Create the title

} else {

}

# Add traces for MAU PCA

  add_trace(x = pca_mau$PC1, y = pca_mau$PC2,
```
